method: Every expectation was written from the sources in src/ by reading them; no analysis tool was run on the sources or on the built inputs, and no tool's detectors or output were looked at. The three inputs are the same program: packed as written, bundled by esbuild, and bundled and minified. Bundling keeps the file names main.js, preload.js, renderer.js and renderer-settings.js, folds ipc-names.js into main.js and preload.js and net.js into renderer.js, and drops the commented-out calls (the bundled input keeps a few comments that sit inside expressions and gains one path comment per source file; the minified input has no comments). Roles are attributed to those four entry files; in this case that is also right for the plain input, because ipc-names.js and net.js hold constants and helper objects only: every IPC call, window, bridge call, request and storage access is written in an entry file. After building, the bundled and the minified files were read to confirm that each expected channel name, address and storage key is still there as a string in the entry file it is attributed to, and that esbuild removed none of the calls (see README.md). An expectation states what the program does, also where that is hard to see (a wrapper, another name for a function, a constant from another file); what only looks like a finding is listed under absent. Negatives that live in a comment exist in the plain input only. webPreferences lists the keys preload, contextIsolation, nodeIntegration and sandbox only and is exhaustive for these four; the source also sets spellcheck on the main window and webSecurity on the settings dialog. A setting is the value the window is really created with: where a later property replaces an earlier one, only the later value is expected.
